title: Platform Engineering, Internal Developer Platforms (IDP) & Developer Portals
summary: Master modern enterprise platform engineering and Internal Developer Platforms (IDP): architecting self-service Golden Paths to replace ticket-based DevOps queues, configuring Backstage software catalogs (catalog-info.yaml) and declarative Scaffolder templates, standardizing workload definitions with Score (score.yaml), and provisioning self-service multi-tenant developer sandboxes with ResourceQuotas and LimitRanges.
learningObjectives: Architect Internal Developer Platforms (IDP) with self-service Golden Paths that reduce cognitive load for application developers.
Configure Backstage software catalog components and declarative software templates for standardized service scaffolding.
Implement Score workload specifications and automated developer sandbox tenant provisioning with strict resource quotas.

curriculumModules.title: Internal Developer Platforms (IDP), Golden Paths & Backstage Catalog
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Platform Engineering treats the underlying cloud and Kubernetes platform as a product, providing paved roads (Golden Paths) that allow application developers to ship code independently without managing Kubernetes primitives. Spotify Backstage unifies software ownership through a centralized Software Catalog (catalog-info.yaml), technical documentation, and Scaffolder templates that automate repository initialization, CI/CD pipelines, and cloud resources with a single click.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Register declarative catalog-info.yaml metadata manifests in application repositories to track microservice ownership, lifecycle stage, and system dependencies in the central developer portal.

curriculumModules.title: Score Workload Specification & Self-Service Tenant Sandboxes
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Infrastructure abstraction requires declarative workload contracts. The Score specification (score.yaml) defines container requirements, environment variables, and resource dependencies without coupling to Kubernetes or cloud-specific syntax; platform orchestrators translate Score files into target environment manifests. To prevent noisy neighbor resource starvation, self-service developer sandboxes enforce namespace isolation paired with strict ResourceQuota and LimitRange compute caps.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Automate self-service developer tenant namespaces provisioned with non-overcommittable CPU/memory ResourceQuotas and default container memory LimitRanges.

labs.title: Backstage Software Catalog Component & Service Ownership Metadata
labs.scenario: Standardize service ownership and architecture metadata in the developer portal: author a Backstage component manifest in /idp/backstage-catalog.yaml defining ConfigMap backstage-catalog-manifest in namespace production with componentName: payment-gateway, componentType: service, lifecycle: production, and owner: team-fintech. Apply to namespace production.
labs.productionContext: Centralized software catalog manifests eliminate orphaned microservices, accelerate incident response by displaying on-call ownership, and automate dependency graph tracking.
objectives: Create namespace production if not present.
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: backstage-catalog-manifest
  namespace: production
data:
  componentName: "payment-gateway"
  componentType: "service"
  lifecycle: "production"
  owner: "team-fintech"
  catalogInfoYaml: "apiVersion: backstage.io/v1alpha1\nkind: Component\nmetadata:\n  name: payment-gateway\nspec:\n  type: service\n  lifecycle: production\n  owner: team-fintech\n"

steps.title: Create production namespace
steps.instruction: Create namespace production if not present.

troubleshootingGuide.problem: ConfigMap missing or metadata fields incorrect.
troubleshootingGuide.cause: ConfigMap must define data.componentName as payment-gateway and data.owner as team-fintech.

labs.title: Self-Service Developer Tenant Sandbox with ResourceQuotas & LimitRanges
labs.scenario: Provision an isolated, self-service developer tenant sandbox for team-alpha: author a manifest in /idp/tenant-sandbox.yaml provisioning namespace sandbox-team-alpha, ResourceQuota sandbox-compute-quota capping requests.cpu to '4000m', requests.memory to '8Gi', and limits.memory to '16Gi', and LimitRange sandbox-limit-range setting default container memory limit to '1Gi'. Apply all manifests to the cluster.
labs.productionContext: Automated tenant sandboxes with quota enforcement give product teams total deployment freedom without risking shared cluster stability or exceeding cloud cloud computing budgets.
objectives: Configure ResourceQuota sandbox-compute-quota with CPU and memory caps.
Configure LimitRange sandbox-limit-range with default memory limit of 1Gi.
Apply all manifests to the cluster.
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: sandbox-team-alpha
  labels:
    platform.kubelabs.io/tier: sandbox
    platform.kubelabs.io/tenant: team-alpha
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: sandbox-compute-quota
  namespace: sandbox-team-alpha
spec:
  hard:
    requests.cpu: "4000m"
    requests.memory: "8Gi"
    limits.memory: "16Gi"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: sandbox-limit-range
  namespace: sandbox-team-alpha
spec:
  limits:
    - type: Container
      default:
        memory: "1Gi"

steps.title: Author tenant sandbox manifest
steps.instruction: Author manifest /idp/tenant-sandbox.yaml defining Namespace, ResourceQuota, and LimitRange.

validationRules.description: ResourceQuota sandbox-compute-quota exists in namespace sandbox-team-alpha
validationRules.name: sandbox-compute-quota
validationRules.remediation: Apply ResourceQuota sandbox-compute-quota in namespace sandbox-team-alpha

validationRules.description: LimitRange sandbox-limit-range exists in namespace sandbox-team-alpha
validationRules.name: sandbox-limit-range
validationRules.remediation: Apply LimitRange sandbox-limit-range in namespace sandbox-team-alpha

solutionCommands:
cat << 'EOF' > /idp/tenant-sandbox.yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: sandbox-team-alpha
  labels:
    platform.kubelabs.io/tier: sandbox
    platform.kubelabs.io/tenant: team-alpha
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ResourceQuota
metadata:
  name: sandbox-compute-quota
  namespace: sandbox-team-alpha
spec:
  hard:
    requests.cpu: "4000m"
    requests.memory: "8Gi"
    limits.memory: "16Gi"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: LimitRange
metadata:
  name: sandbox-limit-range
  namespace: sandbox-team-alpha
spec:
  limits:
    - type: Container
      default:
        memory: "1Gi"
EOF

troubleshootingGuide.problem: ResourceQuota or LimitRange missing or quotas not matching.
troubleshootingGuide.cause: Manifest must create namespace sandbox-team-alpha, ResourceQuota with requests.cpu: 4000m, and LimitRange.

assessmentQuestions.question: What is the primary objective of an Internal Developer Platform (IDP) and 'Golden Paths' in enterprise engineering?
options: To replace all human developers with automated scripts.

To reduce developer cognitive load by providing standardized, self-service infrastructure blueprints that allow product teams to build, deploy, and monitor services autonomously without opening support tickets.
To enforce that all applications use the exact same programming language.
To restrict developers from testing code in local environments.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Platform engineering treats internal platforms as products. Golden Paths offer supported, automated paved roads that eliminate ticket handoffs and cognitive overhead while maintaining organizational governance.

assessmentQuestions.question: How do ResourceQuotas and LimitRanges collaborate to enforce multi-tenant isolation in a shared Kubernetes cluster?
options: ResourceQuotas delete the master nodes if memory is exceeded.

ResourceQuotas place an aggregate cap on total compute resources (CPU/memory requests and limits) a namespace can consume; LimitRanges set min, max, and default resource boundaries per individual container, ensuring pods without explicit resource requests are constrained by default values that conform to the quota.
LimitRanges encrypt network traffic between pods.
assessmentQuestions.explanation: ResourceQuotas cap cumulative compute consumption across the namespace, while LimitRanges enforce individual container defaults and constraints so that unconfigured pods don't exceed namespace allocations.
